questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; standard bibliographies of the named authors

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The only bilingual Ashokan inscription discovered in India's neighbourhood, written in both Greek and Aramaic, is located at
questions.explanation: The Kandahar Bilingual Rock Inscription (Shar-i-Kuna, in modern Afghanistan) is Ashoka's only inscription written simultaneously in Greek and Aramaic. It reflects Ashoka's diplomatic-cultural reach into the Hellenistic and Achaemenid-successor world. Shahbazgarhi (Kharoshthi) and Girnar/Kalsi (Brahmi) are monolingual.
questions.source_citation: D.C. Sircar, Inscriptions of Asoka; Romila Thapar, Asoka and the Decline of the Mauryas

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Kanva dynasty, which briefly ruled Magadha after the fall of the Sungas around 75 BCE, was founded by
questions.explanation: Vasudeva Kanva, a Brahmin minister, overthrew the last Sunga king Devabhuti around 75 BCE to found the Kanva dynasty. The dynasty had four rulers over about 45 years before being displaced by the Satavahanas c. 30 BCE.
questions.source_citation: R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past; Romila Thapar, The Penguin History of Early India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: During the reign of Kanishka I, the Kushana capital was located at
questions.explanation: Kanishka I made Purushapura (modern Peshawar) his capital, from where he ruled a vast empire extending from Central Asia to the Gangetic plain. Mathura was a major second capital and cultural centre under the Kushanas; Taxila was a key intellectual hub in the empire but not its political capital.
questions.source_citation: R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past; A.K. Narain, The Indo-Greeks

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Tamil epic 'Silappadikaram' is traditionally attributed to which author?
questions.explanation: Silappadikaram ('The Tale of an Anklet') is attributed to Ilango Adigal, believed to be the brother of the Chera king Cheran Senguttuvan. Its companion epic, Manimekalai, was authored by Sattanar. Tiruvalluvar composed the Tirukkural; Nakkirar was head of the third Sangam.
questions.source_citation: K.A. Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India; Ilango Adigal, Silappadikaram (tr. R. Parthasarathy)

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Pallava king who avenged the earlier defeat by Chalukyan Pulakesin II and captured the Chalukyan capital Vatapi in 642 CE was
questions.explanation: Narasimhavarman I (r. c. 630-668 CE), also called Mahamalla, defeated and killed Pulakesin II c. 642 CE and captured Vatapi (Badami) — assuming the title 'Vatapikonda'. He also founded the port town of Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram), famous for its rock-cut monuments.
questions.source_citation: K.A. Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: 'Kavirajamarga', the earliest extant literary work in Kannada, was composed under the patronage of which Rashtrakuta king?
questions.explanation: Kavirajamarga ('The Path of Poet-Kings'), a treatise on Kannada poetics, was composed under the patronage of the Rashtrakuta king Amoghavarsha I (r. c. 814-878 CE) in the 9th century. Amoghavarsha himself is sometimes credited as an author. He was a contemporary of Arab travellers like Sulaiman.
questions.source_citation: K.A. Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India; Suryanath U. Kamath, A Concise History of Karnataka

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The teacher and chief adviser of Chandragupta Maurya, traditionally credited with helping him found the Mauryan Empire, was
questions.explanation: Chanakya — also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta — was Chandragupta's teacher and chief adviser. He is credited with authoring the Arthashastra. Vishakhadatta was the playwright of the Mudrarakshasa (which dramatises the Chandragupta-Chanakya story); Megasthenes was the Seleucid ambassador at Chandragupta's court.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Gautama Buddha is believed to have attained enlightenment (Bodhi) at
questions.explanation: Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya (Bihar) under a peepal tree (Bodhi tree). Lumbini (Nepal) is his birthplace; Sarnath is where he gave his first sermon; Kushinagar is where he attained Mahaparinirvana.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; Romila Thapar, The Penguin History of Early India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: India's National Emblem is adapted from the Lion Capital of Ashoka located at
questions.explanation: The National Emblem of India (adopted 26 January 1950) is adapted from the Lion Capital of the Ashokan Pillar at Sarnath, near Varanasi. The pillar was erected to commemorate the site of Buddha's first sermon (Dhamma-chakra-pravartana).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act, 2005

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism was
questions.explanation: Mahavira (Vardhamana), a contemporary of the Buddha, was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism. Rishabhadeva (Adinatha) is the 1st Tirthankara; Parshvanatha is the 23rd; Neminatha is the 22nd. Mahavira was born c. 599 BCE (traditional) near Vaishali.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; P.S. Jaini, The Jaina Path of Purification

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The script used in most of Ashoka's inscriptions across the Indian subcontinent is
questions.explanation: The vast majority of Ashokan inscriptions are in Brahmi. Kharoshthi was used for those in the north-west (e.g., Shahbazgarhi, Mansehra); Aramaic and Greek appear in the north-western Afghan region (Kandahar). Brahmi was deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; D.C. Sircar, Inscriptions of Asoka

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Consider the following statements about the Partition of Bengal (1905):

statements: 1. It was announced by Lord Curzon in July 1905 and came into effect on 16 October 1905.
2. It divided the province into a Muslim-majority East Bengal-and-Assam and a Hindu-majority West Bengal.
3. It was formally annulled in 1912 by Lord Hardinge II.
question_data.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is INCORRECT on the year: the annulment was announced at the Delhi Durbar on 12 December 1911 (Hardinge II), not 1912 — a small but real trap. The 1912 change was the concurrent transfer of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Consider the following statements about the Home Rule Movement in India:

statements: 1. Bal Gangadhar Tilak's Indian Home Rule League was headquartered at Poona.
2. Annie Besant's All-India Home Rule League was headquartered at Madras.
3. The two Leagues formally merged into a single organisation in 1919.
question_data.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — the two leagues operated in different geographical zones with an informal division of work. Statement 3 is INCORRECT: the two leagues never formally merged; both organisations declined in influence after 1918 as the movement was absorbed into the Non-Cooperation agitation.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Consider the following statements about the Cripps Mission (1942):

statements: 1. The Mission promised the grant of dominion status to India after the end of the Second World War.
2. It provided any province with the right to secede from the proposed Indian Union.
3. It offered immediate transfer of power to a national government during the war.
question_data.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — the Cripps proposals promised post-war dominion status and a Constituent Assembly with the right of provinces to opt out (which effectively conceded the Pakistan seed). Statement 3 is INCORRECT: no immediate transfer of power was offered — Gandhi called the offer 'a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank' precisely because of this deferral.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Consider the following statements about the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj):

statements: 1. The INA was first formed in 1942 by Captain Mohan Singh from Indian prisoners of war in Malaya.
2. Rash Behari Bose transferred command of the INA to Subhas Chandra Bose in Singapore on 4 July 1943.
3. The INA fought alongside the Japanese in the Kohima-Imphal campaign of 1944.
question_data.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct — Mohan Singh raised the first INA from PoWs in 1942; Bose took over from Rash Behari Bose in Singapore in July 1943 and later moved to Rangoon; INA units (Subhas Regiment, Gandhi Regiment) fought alongside Japanese forces at Kohima-Imphal in early-mid 1944 before being pushed back.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Peter Ward Fay, The Forgotten Army

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The founder of the Sayyid dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, who took over the throne of Delhi in 1414, was
questions.explanation: Khizr Khan, formerly Timur's deputy at Multan, occupied the Delhi throne in 1414 to found the Sayyid dynasty (1414-1451). He did not assume the title of Sultan and continued to acknowledge Timurid overlordship. He was succeeded by Mubarak Shah, Muhammad Shah IV, and finally Alam Shah, who abdicated to Bahlol Lodi in 1451.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part I

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Bahmani Prime Minister famous for wide-ranging administrative and revenue reforms in the late 15th century, ultimately executed in 1481 on false charges, was
questions.explanation: Mahmud Gawan, an Iranian by origin, served as chief minister (Wakil-us-Sultanat) under Bahmani sultan Muhammad Shah III. He reorganized the four provincial tarafs into eight, standardized revenue measurement, encouraged learning (founded the famous Madrasa at Bidar in 1472), and was executed in 1481 after a factional conspiracy — his death hastened the Bahmani decline.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Which Delhi Sultan formally propounded the theory of kingship as 'Zill-i-Ilahi' (Shadow of God on earth) to elevate the Sultan above the nobility?
questions.explanation: Ghiyasuddin Balban (r. 1266-1287) elaborated the theory of the Sultan as Zill-i-Ilahi (Shadow of God) and Niyabat-i-Khudai (Vice-regent of God on earth) to restore the prestige of the crown, dismantle the power of the Turkan-i-Chihalgani ('The Forty' Turkish nobles established by Iltutmish), and introduce the Persian court practices of sijda (prostration) and paibos (kissing the feet).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part I

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Rana Kumbha, the 15th-century ruler who commissioned the Vijay Stambha (Tower of Victory) at Chittor to commemorate his defeat of Mahmud Khilji of Malwa, belonged to which kingdom?
questions.explanation: Rana Kumbha (r. c. 1433-1468) was the Sisodia ruler of Mewar with capital at Chittor. His nine-storeyed Vijay Stambha (c. 1440s) commemorates the victory over Mahmud Khilji of Malwa at Sarangpur (1437). Kumbha also built the Kirti Stambha, several forts (Kumbhalgarh, Achalgarh), and authored the musical treatise Sangita-raja.
questions.source_citation: Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II; R.C. Majumdar (ed.), The Delhi Sultanate

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The founder of the Mughal Empire in India, who defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526, was
questions.explanation: Zahiruddin Muhammad Babur, ruler of Kabul and descendant of Timur (paternal) and Chinggis Khan (maternal), defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat on 21 April 1526, founding the Mughal (Timurid-Indian) Empire. His autobiography is the Baburnama in Chaghtai Turkish.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Taj Mahal at Agra was commissioned by which Mughal emperor?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan (r. 1628-1658) commissioned the Taj Mahal as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in 1631 at Burhanpur. Construction ran from about 1632 to 1653 under the supervision of Ustad Ahmad Lahori. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 1983).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The founder and first Guru of the Sikh religion was
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak Dev (b. 1469 at Talwandi, now Nankana Sahib in Pakistan; d. 1539 at Kartarpur) was the first of the ten Sikh Gurus and founder of Sikhism. Guru Angad was the second Guru; Guru Arjan the fifth (compiler of the Adi Granth); Guru Gobind Singh the tenth (founder of the Khalsa in 1699).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; J.S. Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Consider the following statements about the Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilization:

statements: 1. The Great Bath, a large public water tank, has been found at Mohenjodaro.
2. Dholavira, one of the largest Harappan sites in India, is located in Gujarat.
3. The Indus script has been fully deciphered and is known to belong to the Indo-Aryan language family.
question_data.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is INCORRECT: the Indus script remains undeciphered despite many attempts, and its linguistic affiliation (Dravidian, Indo-Aryan, or something else) is disputed. Its brief inscriptions (average 5 characters) make decipherment particularly difficult.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Consider the following statements about Ashoka's Dhamma:

statements: 1. Non-violence towards all living beings (ahimsa) was one of its central principles.
2. Special officers called Dhamma-mahamatras were appointed to propagate it and monitor its implementation.
3. Ashoka's personal turn towards Buddhism followed the Kalinga War in the eighth year of his reign.
question_data.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. Rock Edict XIII records the horror of Kalinga and Ashoka's turn to Dhamma; Pillar Edict VII and Rock Edict V mention the Dhamma-mahamatras appointed in the 13th regnal year; ahimsa is a recurring theme across the edicts. Note: 'Dhamma' as Ashoka used it was a broader ethical framework, not identical to Buddhism as a sectarian religion.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; Romila Thapar, Asoka and the Decline of the Mauryas

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Match List-I (Ancient Indian dynasty) with List-II (Founder) and select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya (c. 321 BCE) founded the Mauryas; Pushyamitra Sunga (c. 185 BCE) founded the Sungas after killing Brihadratha; Vasudeva Kanva (c. 75 BCE) founded the Kanvas after overthrowing Devabhuti; Simuka (c. 1st century BCE) is traditionally regarded as the founder of the Satavahana dynasty.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Match List-I (Ancient Indian text) with List-II (Author) and select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Panini composed the Ashtadhyayi (Sanskrit grammar, c. 5th-4th century BCE); Patanjali wrote the Mahabhashya (a commentary on Panini, c. 2nd century BCE); Kautilya authored the Arthashastra (c. 4th century BCE); Kalidasa wrote Meghaduta (Gupta age, c. 4th-5th century CE).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; A.L. Basham, The Wonder That Was India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Match List-I (Tribal or peasant uprising against British rule) with List-II (Principal leader) and select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu led the Santhal Hool; Birsa Munda led the Ulgulan among the Mundas; Buddhu Bhagat was a key leader of the Kol Rebellion in Chotanagpur; Govind Guru led the Bhil movement culminating in the Mangarh massacre of 17 November 1913 in Rajasthan-Gujarat border.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; K.S. Singh, Tribal Movements in India

questions.body: Match List-I (Viceroy) with List-II (Event associated with the tenure) and select the correct answer using the code given below:

list_2: 3. Assassination of Rand by the Chapekar brothers (1897)
4. Resignation over the Baroda Gaekwad case (1875-76)

questions.explanation: Lord Mayo was assassinated by Sher Ali Afridi at Port Blair on 8 February 1872; Northbrook resigned in 1876 over disagreement on the Baroda Gaekwad Malhar Rao's trial and abdication; Age of Consent Act (1891) was passed during Lansdowne's tenure; the Chapekar brothers assassinated W.C. Rand at Poona (June 1897) during Elgin II's Viceroyalty.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Consider the following statements about the iqta system of the Delhi Sultanate:

statements: 1. An iqta was an assignment of the right to collect revenue from a specified area in return for military and civil service.
2. Iltutmish organised the iqta system as a systematic form of administrative-revenue arrangement in the Delhi Sultanate.
3. Firuz Shah Tughlaq made iqtas hereditary.
question_data.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. Iqtas were assignments of revenue rights (not land ownership) tied to service; Iltutmish gave the system its organised Sultanate form; Firuz Shah Tughlaq allowed iqtas to be inherited by descendants — a step that weakened central control and encouraged the trend towards heritable jagirs in later periods.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part I

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Match List-I (Mughal emperor) with List-II (Major architectural work commissioned or completed during his reign) and select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Babur ordered the Kabuli Bagh Mosque at Panipat (c. 1527) to commemorate his 1526 victory; Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri (1571-1585) with the Buland Darwaza added after the Gujarat conquest; Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal (1632-53); Aurangzeb's son Prince Azam Shah built Bibi Ka Maqbara (c. 1660s-1670s) as a tribute to his mother Dilras Banu Begum.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Catherine Asher, Architecture of Mughal India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Consider the following statements about Mahatma Gandhi's leadership of Indian mass movements:

statements: 1. The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was Gandhi's first Satyagraha campaign in India.
2. The Salt March (Dandi March) began at Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930.
3. Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942.
question_data.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

questions.explanation: All three statements are correct — Champaran (1917) was Gandhi's first Indian Satyagraha; the Dandi March started at Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 and reached Dandi on 6 April 1930; the Quit India Resolution was passed on 8 August 1942 at Bombay's Gowalia Tank Maidan.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Match List-I (Leader) with List-II (Slogan popularly associated with them) and select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: 'Inquilab Zindabad' — famously shouted by Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt in the Central Legislative Assembly (April 1929); 'Jai Hind' — Subhas Chandra Bose's INA salutation; 'Do or Die' — Gandhi's call at Gowalia Tank (August 1942); 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' — Lal Bahadur Shastri's rallying cry during the 1965 Indo-Pak War.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; standard biographies of the named leaders

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Match List-I (River) with List-II (Ancient city situated on it) and select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Pataliputra (Patna) is on the Ganga; Mathura is on the Yamuna; Amaravati (Satavahana capital) is on the Krishna; Thanjavur (Chola capital) is on the Kaveri.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935:

statements: 1. It abolished dyarchy at the provincial level.
2. It introduced dyarchy at the Centre for the proposed federation.
3. It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court, which was set up in 1937.
4. It introduced universal adult franchise for elections to the provincial legislatures.
question_data.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — dyarchy at the provinces (1919) was abolished and provincial autonomy introduced; dyarchy was to be introduced at the Centre under the federal plan (though the federal part never came into effect); the Federal Court was set up at Delhi on 1 October 1937. Statement 4 is INCORRECT — the franchise was expanded to about 30 million (14% of adult population), far short of universal.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Match List-I (Sangam-period Tamil literary work or collection) with List-II (Description) and select the correct answer using the code given below:

list_2: 3. Collection of Eight Anthologies of Shorter Poems
4. The earliest surviving Tamil grammar treatise

questions.explanation: Ettuthogai comprises Eight Anthologies (e.g., Ainkurunuru, Purananuru, Akananuru); Pattupattu is the collection of Ten Long Idylls (e.g., Mullaippattu, Maduraikanci); Tolkappiyam by Tolkappiyar is the earliest surviving Tamil grammatical treatise; Silappadikaram (by Ilango Adigal) and Manimekalai (by Sattanar) are the twin post-Sangam Tamil epics.
questions.source_citation: K.A. Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India; Kamil Zvelebil, The Smile of Murugan
